text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello! I'm Gemma. Can you hear me?
B: Hello! Yes, I can hear you. I'm Karen. Sorry, I've still got my lanyard on, I keep forgetting to take it off.
A: [laughs] I saw that in your photo, the badge was the wrong way round. I do exactly the same, I've gone to Tesco in mine before.
B: Oh, I've done Tesco in mine loads. Where are you?
A: Beeston, near Nottingham. You?
B: Basingstoke. Not very exciting, but it's home, you know.
A: Aw, no, it's nice to be from somewhere. What do you do, Karen?
B: Admin, at a building maintenance firm. I book the engineers in, answer the phones. I'm honestly a bit hopeless at the organising bit, to be fair, my desk is just Post-it notes. I'm better on the phone. Someone's ringing up because their ceiling's leaking and they're crying, and I'm quite good at that, calming people down, you know. It's the confirmation emails I forget.
A: Oh, but the calming down is the hard bit! You can't teach that. I'm a pharmacy technician and I've got colour-coded checklists for everything, but if a nurse is stressed I'm the one going "right, okay, deep breath."
B: Colour-coded! I'd love that. Could you come and do my desk?
A: [laughs] I would actually enjoy that, which says a lot about me.
B: Have you got kids? Sorry, I always ask that, I'm a mum, it just comes out.
A: No, go on! One, Isla, she's six. You?
B: Callum, he's fourteen. Growing out of school trousers every five minutes. I bought new ones in September and they're halfway up his shins already.
A: Oh no! Isla's the same with shoes. Does he go to his dad's?
B: Every other weekend, mostly. And my mum helps with lifts, I don't know what I'd do without her. Her knee's playing up at the minute, though.
A: My mum does two pick-ups for us. I worry about her, to be honest, since my dad died. She's on her own with this mardy old Jack Russell.
B: Aw. I lost my dad too. You sort of keep an eye on them more, don't you?
A: You do, yeah. Sorry, that got serious. Erm, do you bake? I feel like you bake.
B: [laughs] A Victoria sponge for birthdays. That's my one thing.
A: I did a lemon drizzle for church on Sunday and it sank right in the middle. Like a crater. I filled it with icing and hoped nobody'd notice.
B: That's what icing's for! Did they notice?
A: The vicar had two slices, so no.
B: There you go then. What are you having for your dinner tonight?
A: Tea? Oh, it's a veggie chilli, it's in the freezer, labelled. Sorry, "tea", that's a Nottingham thing.
B: I'll be in Tesco at half six staring at the shelves, probably. Fajita kit, maybe.
A: Honestly, that's a perfectly good tea.
